author: pgaudet
body:
Following up on https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/29238#issuecomment-4844011524

> Inhibition of host TRAFs by virus (https://www.uniprot.org/keywords/KW-1110)
maps to GO:0039527 symbiont-mediated suppression of host TRAF-mediated signal transduction, but the parent of KW-1110 refers to a specific pathway, Inhibition of host RLR pathway by virus (KW-1113)

> Could the mapping be moved to [symbiont-mediated suppression of host cytoplasmic pattern recognition receptor signaling pathway via inhibition of TRAF activity](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_0140476) ? 

@pmasson55 replied: 
> Yes we should moved the term to a better hierarchy since TRAFs plays role in various processes including TLRs or cGAS-STING pathway and not only on RLR pathway.
RLRs (RIG-I-like receptors) are cytosolic RNA sensors: RIG-I (DDX58), MDA5 (IFIH1), and LGP2 (DHX58). They detect viral RNA in the cytoplasm and signal through the adaptor MAVS on the mitochondrial membrane, driving TBK1/IRF3 and NF‑κB activation.
title: Update KW-1110 Inhibition of host TRAFs by virus GO mapping
